title: Fin-steered model rocket
note: Our own design, not a kit: a BT-70-size airframe on an Estes F15 with four all-moving fins, each turned by an AGFRC C04CLS servo through a pushrod, flown by the rocket-recorder board. Tube, motor-mount and motor sizes are sourced; the nose and fin shapes are design values.

body_length.quote: 56mm x 18" Body Tube: two 18" tubes joined (design: two standard lengths)

motor_diameter.quote: F15 29 114 0-4-6-8 .0600 .10300 E (diameter mm, length mm, delays, propellant kg, total kg)

nose_length.note: tangent ogive, 2 body diameters (3 looked too pointed), its tip rounded (nose_tip_radius)

overall_length.note: body plus nose, plus the motor tube and retainer cap standing out aft (mount_overhang + retainer_lip)

fins.quote: Repeat these steps for all four fins (a 4-fin BT-70-size kit)

fin_hinge.value: all-moving, pivot at the quarter of the mean aerodynamic chord
fin_hinge.quote: Barrowman's method assumes that the lengthwise position of the CP stays at a constant 25% of the MAC at subsonic speeds (a pivot there keeps the servo's load small: design)

flight_computer.quote: servo_headers block: four servo outputs on GPIO 8-11 (PWM 4A, 4B, 5A, 5B)

fin_sweep.note: leading edge, root to tip, along the axis

fin_root_te_height.note: root trailing edge above the tube's base

retainer.value: 29 mm screw-on retainer: a threaded ring epoxied over the motor tube's aft end and a cap that screws on over the motor's rim
retainer.quote: INSTALL ENGINE RETAINER ... Apply epoxy to the outside of tube A ... With the notched side of H facing in towards the rocket, place H over tube A (page 6); parts list: 29mm engine retainer set

retainer_material.quote: molded from heat-resistant ABS plastic to withstand repeated flights. Compatible with Estes E16 and F15 motors

mount_overhang.source: design, chosen: the motor tube stands out aft of the body for the retainer, as tube A does in the kit's instructions (page 6 drawing)

retainer_thread_od.source: design, estimate: sizes not published; shape from Estes' retainer photo (estes_retainer)

retainer_cap_od.source: design, estimate: sizes not published; 16 flats as in Estes' photo

retainer_lip_id.source: design, estimate: smaller than the 29 mm motor so the lip holds its rim

motor_wall.source: design, estimate: casing wall thickness not published

nozzle_recess.source: design, estimate: F15 nozzle geometry not published

nozzle_length.source: design, estimate: F15 nozzle geometry not published

nozzle_exit_d.source: design, estimate: F15 nozzle geometry not published

nozzle_throat_d.source: design, estimate: F15 nozzle geometry not published

lug_id.note: 3/16 in; the kit's own lug (038181) is not tied to a size; the kit page gives the rod as 3/16 in. (4.78 mm)

lugs.value: two, between fins, each even with the aft end of a body tube
lugs.quote: Measure the center between the fins on the bottom of tube C the bottom of tube I ... Even with the end of tube. ... Place the launch lugs ensuring that align between the middle of the fins (page 6)

lettering.source: design, chosen: the payload's name, set in Geist (geist_font), twice: on the lines of fins 1 and 3 (fin0 and fin2), each reading up from just above its fin; mask refs/finrocket/lettering-mask.png drawn from the font with PIL ("Altair" at 190 px, "ULTRALIGHT PAYLOAD" 40% smaller at 114 px, on one baseline)

lettering_length.source: design, chosen: the mask's 1809 x 250 px sheet at the lettering's height

lettering_height.source: design, chosen: letters of "Altair" about 20 mm tall

lettering_font.quote: This Font Software is licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1

lettering_gap.source: design, chosen: the lettering starts this far above the fin's root leading edge

nose_tip_radius.source: design, chosen: a rounded tip, as moulded model-rocket nose cones have

fin_tip_band.source: design, chosen: a thin red line along each fin's tip

roll_pattern.value: thin black rings at stage joints, black panels below each ring and a black stripe at the base, all on one side, one above another
roll_pattern.quote: Carrying the Apollo 11 Saturn V rocket and mobile launcher, the crawler inches its way along the three-and-a-half-mile journey to Launch Pad 39A.
roll_pattern.note: read from the photo: S-IC base stripe between the USA letters, ring and panel at the S-IC's top, ring and panel at the S-IVB's aft end

roll_ring_height.source: design, chosen: thin, as the Saturn V's rings are against its stages

roll_panel_arc_deg.source: design, estimate: the Saturn V's panels look about an eighth of the way round in nasa_as11_rollout (about 0.45 of the visible width)

flag.value: the US flag, upright, on the lines of fins 1 and 3 just below the joint ring, above the lettering, as on the Saturn V
flag.quote: Current RGB colors and geometric specifications follow the [State Department] Design Guide ... The geometric specifications for the Union and the star sizes and placement come from an attachment to Executive Order 10834
flag.note: masks refs/finrocket/flag-*.png redrawn from the SVG's geometry (7410 x 3900, stripes 300, union 2964 x 2100, stars of radius 120 on a 494 x 420 grid) at 1/5

flag_hoist.source: design, chosen: the flag's height; its fly is 1.9 times it (us_flag's 7410 x 3900)

flag_gap.source: design, chosen: below the joint ring

flight.note: what /circuits/fly simulates; masses and the centre of gravity are estimates, everything else sourced

also.quote: Total Impulse 49.61 N-sec ... Max Thrust 25.26 Newtons (5.7 lbs) Thrust Duration 3.45 Seconds ... Weight 3.66 oz. (103.8 g) Propellant Weight 2.12 oz. (60.0 g)

dry_mass.note: the Black Brant XII's 326 g (estes_bbxii: "Weight 11.5 oz. (326 g)") scaled to this rocket's 1.08 m from its 1.386 m ("Length 54.6 in. (138.62 cm)"), plus 4 servos at 4.5 g (agf_c04cls: "Net Weight 4.5 g") and the board and a battery (estimated 30 g; the battery isn't chosen)

cg_from_nose.note: forward of the Black Brant XII's aft limit in proportion (estes_bbxii: "DO NOT fly model rocket with the center of gravity further back than 38.69 in. from the tip of the nose cone", 0.71 of its length); this rocket's 0.5636 m is 0.55 of its 1.027 m (0.62 m before the nose was shortened by 5.64 cm)

cd.quote: A typical value for the drag coefficient of a model rocket is .75, based on the cross-sectional area of the rocket.

fin_max_deg.quote: if emfg were greater than 10°, the saturation value, the control surfaces would be unable to stop the rocket from rolling (their control surfaces stop at 10°; used here as the fins' travel)

rail_length.note: a 1 m launch rod; the kit's "Launch Rod Size 3/16 in." gives no length

aero.quote: nose: (3.19) CNα = 2/Aref [A(l) − A(0)], CP (3.28) X = [l A(l) − V] / [A(l) − A(0)]; one fin (3.40) (CNα)1 = 2π (s²/Aref) / (1 + sqrt(1 + (β s²/(Afin cos Γc))²)); four fins N/2 times that (3.53); body interference (3.55) KT(B) = 1 + rt/(s + rt); fin CP at 25% of the MAC; total CP by the moment sum (3.29)

open_questions: Battery not chosen: its mass is in the 30 g estimate.
Dry mass and centre of gravity are estimates until the parts are weighed.
No dimensioned fin template exists for the Black Brant XII; fin shape is a design value.
F15 nozzle sizes (exit, throat, recess) and casing wall are not published: design estimates until a motor is measured.
Retainer sizes are estimates from Estes' photo; the kit's launch lug size is not stated (3/16 x 2 in from the lug pack).
